text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic says in New York he expects Yugoslav sanctions to be lifted early this week.
- Yugoslav and Croatian missing persons commissions to meet in Belgrade on October 2-3.
- Head of the Serb government in eastern Slavonia Vojislav Stanimirovic says exodus of Serbs from the area has been halted and that an increasing number of people are coming to settle there.

- Yugoslav airlines JAT will soon resume flights to the U.S., says Yugoslav transport and communications minister Zoran Vujovic after talks with officials of the American Federal Aviation Agency (FAA).
- Meat product prices rose considerably over the past week.
- Firm budgetary limitations have been set and all expenditure is being financed solely from real sources, says Serbian finance minister Dusan Vlatkovic.
- The federal government plans to appoint honorary consuls in 67 countries of the world.
- Former Yugoslav central bank governor Dragoslav Avramovic to head the election list of opposition coalition Zajedno (Together).
- "After winning federal elections I will accept the post of Prime Minister," says Dragoslav Avramovic, former Yugoslav central bank governor.
- The Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) forms an election coalition with the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) and the New Democracy (ND) parties.
- Belgrade Surcin airport was reopened on Saturday after reconstruction of the runway was completed.
- Serbian finance minister Dusan Vlatkovic says teachers will receive back pay before October 1 as promised by the Serbian government.
- This year's corn crop expected to be around 6 million tonnes says Lazar Jakovljevic of the Novi Sad crop farming institute.
- Following new bout of terrorist attacks in Kosovo on Friday the Serbian police still looking for perpetrators.
